thread.title: Apple: Here’s a Glimpse at Its Next Round of Products

author: David Marino-Nachison
title: Apple: Here’s a Glimpse at Its Next Round of Products
text:
Photo: Getty Images The future of several Apple products is coming into clearer view, with news organizations and analysts recently reporting information that offers more detail about what 2018 could bring for the company’s phones, tablets and other devices.
Some highlights:
• A Bloomberg report, published Monday , shared details about expected changes to the iPhone lineup, including: A new phone the same size as the iPhone X, which has turned in disappointing sales ; A lower-end model that includes some of the newer phones’ features, such as facial recognition; and one with a screen that would be one of the largest available, as Jonathan Swartz noted for Barron’s . (Earlier this month, we shared one analysis of how potential changes to the iPhone lineup could shake up sales at Apple.)
• A closely followed analyst recently published a note, reported by AppleInsider , that said Barron’s Next 50 stock Apple 
(AAPL) could debut a line of new over-the-ear headphones. (The company also owns the Beats brand after an acquisition in 2014.) • And new AirPod headphones could let users activate Apple’s Siri digital assistant simply by saying her name aloud, rather than by touching them. (A model expected in 2019, a Bloomberg report said , could be water-resistant.)
• Let’s not forget recent reports about a wireless charging mat, also covered by Swartz , that could launch in March. Or another Bloomberg report that hinted at a new iPad due later this year. (We recently reported on 2017 tablet sales figures , where Apple is battling Samsung and Amazon.com (AMZN).) 
Or, for that matter, the fact that Apple has already launched a completely new product, its HomePod smart speaker , this year.
• If all that doesn’t interest you—but you’re nevertheless hankering for some Apple news—we direct you to a story from the Guardian , in which musician Moby explains how company executives “handed me the first iPod and said: ‘Steve [Jobs] wanted you to have this.’ I said: ‘You do know at some point this is going to have a camera and a phone attached to it?’ And they laughed at me and said that could never happen.”
